title: Countermovement jump: the typical error
intro:
Illustrative data, made up for this book: the sizes and patterns are realistic, the teams and players are not real. Eighteen players did a countermovement jump test twice in a session; the values are the differences (cm), trial 2 minus trial 1.

Give the mean difference (two decimals) and the standard deviation of the differences (three decimals). The **typical error** of one test is that standard deviation divided by √2; the Learn page uses it to judge whether a player's change is real.

In the Workbench: **Descriptive statistics**, paste the differences.
hints: A mean near 0 means no learning or fatigue between trials; the SD measures the noise.
